primary_task: Audit one marketing page (given as an HTML file or URL) for conversion issues and reply with a scored CRO report organised as Quick Wins, High-Impact Changes, Test Ideas and Copy Alternatives.

requirements.name: python3
requirements.evidence: `python3 scripts/conversion_audit.py --file page.html` ... Run it before the manual framework pass; its score anchors the audit ... Open with the `conversion_audit.py` score
requirements.basis: "bash": "run shell commands on Linux x86_64: install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads), build, test, run CLIs and scripts, git, gh, start and stop local servers inside the session; network requests reach only the allow-listed hosts"

requirements.name: scripts/conversion_audit.py (skill-bundled script)
requirements.evidence: | Conversion audit | `python3 scripts/conversion_audit.py --file page.html` (or `--url https://...`; `--json` for pipelines) |
requirements.basis: The manifest does not say whether skill-bundled scripts are present; "skill": "load an installed Claude Code skill, list and search skills and plugins" suggests the installed skill folder is readable. Check that scripts/conversion_audit.py exists in the installed skill.

requirements.name: the marketing page's host (when given as --url)
requirements.evidence: (or `--url https://...`; `--json` for pipelines) -- alternative to `--file page.html`
requirements.basis: "web_fetch": "fetch a web page or unauthenticated API by URL; hosts outside the egress allow-list are refused" -- whether a given page's host is reachable depends on the host; the --file path avoids it.

requirements.name: .claude/product-marketing-context.md
requirements.evidence: If `.claude/product-marketing-context.md` exists, read it before asking questions.
requirements.basis: "read": "read files in the working directory; search them by name pattern or content (glob, grep)"

notes: Took the reading that the audit script run is a required step ("Run it before the manual framework pass"; output must "Open with the conversion_audit.py score"). Its presence is unknown (not stated by the manifest); if the script is missing, the scored opening cannot be produced but the manual framework analysis still can. If the user supplies only a URL on a host outside the allow-list (e.g. a company site), fetching fails and the page would have to be supplied as a file; under that reading the egress requirement would become hard and unavailable, giving BLOCKED. Unknowns: script presence, page host.
